properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: ARMAC RESOURCES LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 3/13/2023
Violation Code: 78.88(d) - OPERATING WELLS - MECHANICAL INTEGRITY OF OPERATING WELLS - Operator failed to immediately notify the Department and take corrective actions to repair or replace defective equipment or casing for wells exhibiting progressive corrosion, rusting or other signs of equipment deterioration that compromise the integrity of the well.
Violation ID: 988191
Permit API: 123-45286
Unconventional: No
County: Warren
Municipality: Warren City
Inspection Type: Compliance Evaluation
Inspection Date: 3/13/2023
Comments: This well was inspected as part of an on going gas migration case. At the time of inspection I observed a cable rig rigged up over the well and the well shut in. There was an odor of gas emitting from the well and I could visually see gas bubbling behind the tubing at surface. A slam bar hole was placed 1.5' from the well and was metered with and ALTAIR 5X five sensor meter. At this slam bar hole 100% methane was detected. I then put a series of slam bar holes (12 total) radiating outward from the well. At points 50' from the well no gas was detected. I spoke with Justin Hanson of Bull Run Energy who does all the well tending in this area for Armac and he stated that they were going to run a cement bond log on this well tomorrow (03/14/2023).

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 7/22/2024 to CHESAPEAKE APPALACHIA LLC in Asylum Township, Bradford county. 78a85(a)5 - CASING AND CEMENTING - CEMENT STANDARDS - The operator failed to prevent gas flow in the annulus.  In areas of known shallow gas producing zones, gas block additives and low fluid loss slurries shall be used.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: CHESAPEAKE APPALACHIA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 7/22/2024
Violation Code: 78a85(a)5 - CASING AND CEMENTING - CEMENT STANDARDS - The operator failed to prevent gas flow in the annulus. In areas of known shallow gas producing zones, gas block additives and low fluid loss slurries shall be used.
Violation ID: 8195330
Permit API: 015-21313
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Asylum Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 7/22/2024
Comments: Weather was 74¿¿ and cloudy. There were no Chesapeake representatives on location at time of inspection. Well appeared to be capable of production. Well had digital pressure monitoring equipment attached reading 1 PSI on the well head and -3 PSI on the production casing. Well had 2 annulus vents plumbed to the production tank with digital pressure monitoring equipment attached. The surface casing (13 3/8") X intermediate casing (9 5/8") annulus vent read 0 PSI and the intermediate casing (9 5/8") X production casing (5 1/2") annulus vent read 5 PSI. During the inspection, the 13 3/8" X 9 5/8" annulus vent was opened to atmosphere and 78% LEL and 6% Methane/Volume was detected. Creston arrived onsite and detected combustible gas (e.g., bubbling) in the cellar and on the 13 3/8" X 9 5/8" annulus vent. No gas was observed leaking from the wellhead during the inspection. In an email dated 7/25/2024, Chesapeake provided the following information after further evaluating the stray gas observed during the inspection: "As per our conversation, the well head crew observed minimal, intermittent bubbles in cellar. Bubbling was not confined to one area and appeared to be coming from various spots. GM site truck pulled water and FMC wellhead techs moved in to inspect wellhead components and piping for leaks. NO GAS leaks detected Pressure test 5-1/2"x 9-5/8" hanger seals to 1500 psi- GOOD test Pressure test 9-5/8"x13-3/8" hanger seals to 1500 psi- GOOD test They secured well head. LEL 50%- 90% detected in the 13-3/8" vent line." The Department's investigation of the Hopson 5H well found that combustible gas is currently venting outside of the surface casing string. This is a violation of the Department's regulations relating to Cement Standards, 25 Pa. Code ¿¿78a.85(a)(5), which provides: "When cementing surface casing or coal protective casing, the operator shall use cement that meets or exceeds the ASTM International C 150, Type I, II, or III Standard or API Specification 10. The cement must also: (5) Prevent gas flow in the annulus. In areas of known shallow gas producing zones, gas block additives and low fluid loss slurries shall be used." The Department’s investigation of the Hopson 5H well also detected the presence of combustible gas at the 13 3/8" X 9 5/8" annulus vent. This is a violation of the Department’s regulations relating to Defective Cement, 25 Pa. Code ¿¿78a.86, which provides "In a well that has defective, insufficient or improperly cemented casing, the operator shall report the defect to the Department within 24 hours of discovery by the operator and shall correct the defect. The operator shall correct the defect or submit a plan to correct the defect for approval by the Department within 30 days. If the defect cannot be corrected or an alternate method is not approved by the Department, the well shall be plugged under ¿¿ 78.91 – 78.98 (related to plugging)." Please provide a written response detailing how Chesapeake intends to comply with this regulation, including information regarding the suspected source of stray gas, by 8/23/2024.

Report Details

Violation Code: 78a54 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS - Operator failed to control and dispose of fluids, residual waste and drill cuttings, including tophole water, brines, drilling fluids, drilling muds, stimulation fluids, well servicing fluids, oil, and production fluids in a manner that prevents pollution of the waters of the Commonwealth and in accordance with 25 Pa. Code §§ 78a.55 – 78a.58 and 78a.60 – 78a.63.
Violation ID: 922307
Permit API: 125-27785
Unconventional: Yes
County: Washington
Municipality: Somerset Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 6/28/2021
Comments: On June 28, 2021, I conducted an inspection of the Papa Bear Well Site in Somerset Township, Washington County. The inspection was conducted in response to a release of fluid reported to the Department on 6/25/2021. On 6/25/2021, the Operator reported that more than 5 gallons of produced water was spilled to the well pad from a Gas Production Unit dump line. At the time of inspection, SPSI and Moody and Associates were in the process of remediating the impacted material and flushing the well pad drains. The Moody and Associates representative Jona Stosky indicated that the operator would be utilizing Act 2 clean up standards for brine. The remediation crew has excavated the well pad drain trench on the east side of the well pad. The trench was excavated directly behind the Gas Production Units (GPU). The trench appeared to be 5’ wide, 45’ long and approximately 3’ in depth. Ms. Stosky indicated that approximately 90 yards of impacted material has been removed from the well pad and placed in roll off disposal boxes. Ms. Stosky indicated that additional material may need to be removed to remediate the well pad. I observed staining on the dump line associated with the GPU labeled as the 10H. The remediation crew was flushing and or washing the well pad drain and the area under the 10H GPU unit with fresh water to flush out the production fluid. On 6/29/2021, I spoke with EQT representative David Crayne., Mr. Crayne indicated that approximately 42 gallons of production fluid was released. The spill appeared to be contained on the well pad. Violations are being issued in relation to the release of a regulated material.

Violation ID: 980670
Permit API: 129-27065
Unconventional: No
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: North Huntingdon Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 1/04/2023
Comments: On January 4, 2023, the Department conducted an inspection at the Bozich 2 well site in North Huntingdon Township, Westmoreland County. Present were myself and DEP OGI Patrick Hiles. The purpose of this inspection was to follow up to IR 3453961, during which remediation efforts were made by the operator in response to IR 3446144, where impacted soil was discovered by the Department.The following was observed:The well site excavation has been backfilled since IR 3453961 (see photos 2 and 5). The site appeared to be stabile with no concerns related to accelerated erosion or sedimentation, and was mulched and seeded. The excavation stockpile remains placed atop a sheet of black plastic (see photo 1). However, it was uncovered unlike the operator and contractor reported. The well head was equipped with a well tag (see photo 3). The brine tank appeared to be sound at the time of inspection, with no evidence of leaks or discharge (see photo 4). Soil conductivity readings were taken around the excavation stockpile to ensure that contamination has not leached into the ground. Elevated conductivity was found immediately downslope of the stockpile, on its west side (see photos 6, 7, and 9). Additional readings were taken approximately 4 feet further downslope from this point, and around the rest of the stockpile (see photos 8, 10, 11, and 12). No additional elevated readings were gathered. Soil conductivity readings were also taken in the backfilled area around the brine tank, which appeared to be comparable to the surrounding soil (see photos 13, 14, and 15). A background soil conductivity reading was taken in the crop field east of the well site, which read 170 Microsiemens (see photo 16). Based on observations from this inspection, the impacted soil appears to have been excavated from the area of release. However, the contaminants contained within the excavation stockpile appear to be washing downslope into the surrounding soil, and is therefore not being properly stored and/or contained. Because this contamination appears to be localized close to the stockpile, the Department recommends immediate remediation and proper storage to prevent the contamination from spreading. Also, the Department once again requests an approximate quantity released from the brine tank, and the waste manifest when available.

Soil conductivity readings were also taken in the backfilled area around the brine tank, which appeared to be comparable to the surrounding soil (see photos 13, 14, and 15). A background soil conductivity reading was taken in the crop field east of the well site, which read 170 Microsiemens (see photo 16). However, the contaminants contained within the excavation stockpile appear to be washing downslope into the surrounding soil, and is therefore not being properly stored and/or contained. Comments: On 04/12/2021, Department of Environmental Protection ("DEP") representative John Ciccone completed an administrative inspection report on Chesapeake Appalachia LLC’s ("CALLC") RAINBOW location at 0916 hours. This administrative inspection was completed in response to results for sample ID # 9544-045 becoming available on 04/11/2021. Sample ID # 9544-045 was collected from CALLC’s RAINBOW location on 03/22/2021 from a puddle on the pad surface with a field measured specific conductivity of approximately 7 mS/cm. A sample of 125mL of fluid was collected and submitted for SAC 942 + Al, Li analysis on 03/23/2021. Details regarding the 03/22/2021 site visit can be found within inspection report # 3166117. Constituents of concern are as follows: Barium was reported at 51.64 mg/L Lithium was reported at 3.382 mg/L Strontium was reported at 5.42 mg/L Aluminum was reported at 94.92 mg/L Manganese was reported at 6.353 mg/L Iron was reported at 198.6 mg/L Elevated levels of heavy metals are indicative of a release of production and/or flowback fluids to the pad surface. Due to the results of sample ID # 9544-045, violations related to the release of production / flowback fluids to the pad surface are cited against well permit # 015-23616. A violation of 25 Pa. Code 78a.56a ("TEMPORARY STORAGE"), Clean Streams Law, Section 402(b), Solid Waste Management Act, Section 301, and 25 Pa. Code 78a.66 ("REPORTING AND REMEDIATING SPILLS AND RELEASES") have been cited.

Comments: On 01/14/2025 a representative from the Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a routine inspection of Greylock Production LLC's Ron multi-well pad located in Hector Township, Potter County. Upon arrival to the site at 1000 hours, weather was 16F and partly cloudy. An Act 9 sign is visible and located at the site entrance (photo #1).All standing water observed on the pad surface was frozen solid.Hydraulic fracturing activities for the 2 wells located onsite have been completed and flow back is scheduled to begin soon prior to placing the wells into production; the well permits are posted alongside the Act 9 sign (photos #1 and 2). The gas processing units (GPUs) and produced fluids tanks for the wells have been installed onsite and are not yet in use, all production equipment is held in secondary containment and the produced fluids tanks are not yet labeled (photos #3 and 4).The upright brine storage tanks which were used during hydraulic fracturing remain onsite and are held on containment (photo #5). 2 modular aboveground storage structures (MASS) remain onsite to hold brine for hydraulic fracturing and flow back; rig matting is installed at the offload area of the MASS's as secondary containment (phots #6 and 7). 10 temporary storage tanks were also noted onsite to hold brine and produced fluids during flow back; these tanks are held in secondary containment (photo #8). All diesel tanks observed onsite to power heavy machinery were held in containment (photo #9).Site stabilization could not be adequately assessed due to snow coverage. No accelerated erosion or sedimentation was observed. 1 infiltration basin serves as the site's post construction stormwater management (PCSM) control (photo #10). No standing water was observed in the PCSM controls and they appear to be functioning as intended.The DEP recommends the following:-Labeling the produced fluids tanks prior to them being put into use for production.The violations noted in inspection report #'s 3881391 and 3878285 remain outstanding against API #105-21962No violations noted. I departed the site at 1100 hours.

The well tag that was affixed to the well head during the time of IR 3944466 appears to have been removed. No staining or distressed vegetation was observed on the ground around the well head (see photo 6). The additional piping and production equipment that does not appear to be in use remains onsite (see photo 7). The Department recommends that equipment onsite that is not in use for production is removed from site. The well postings onsite include contact information for Dorso LP (see photos 8 and 9).Based on observations from this inspection, violations that were continued from IR 3944466 shall remain outstanding, as it appears that no corrective action has been taken onsite since the date of that inspection and no response of any kind to IR 3093059 has been received to date.

Violation ID: 922661
Permit API: 053-27124
Unconventional: No
County: Forest
Municipality: Howe Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 7/08/2021
Comments: Responded to a call from Minard Run to Scott Motter ( Dep representative) in regards that there had been a crude oil spill at one of there tank batteries in Forest County, Howe Township PA. Upon arriving on location I met with Minard Run Representative Gary Davis and USFS Mike Lewis. They gave a brief run down of the incident and work that had been completed to stop the flow of Crude Oil. There was a failure at well 053-27124. A valve broke which was connected to a steel line on the exit side of the check valve, which is going to tank battery. Minard Run is on site. A new valve was installed. Booms and pads were in place at the time of my arrival. They are Currently digging diversion ditches and a siphon dam. Crude product left the well site, traveled the road ditch, and went through a culvert. At that point some of the product went into a fresh water pond and some oil diverted around the pond into a wet land and then into a wooded area. Once it entered the wooded area the product penetrated the large rock structure area and flowed underground to the fresh water tributary. Pictures show where Minard Run placed booms to attempt to stop the flow down stream. The flow is carrying some product further down stream, in which they have more booms in place. It was approx estimate of 2 to 3 barrels of crude leaked. Minard Run was going to try to get a volume of the gathering lines to help identify the volume. It was suggested to add additional booms down stream and continue with the current clean up process. In light of future rains tonight it was suggested to leave booms in-place and remove pads to prevent them being pushed down stream. Minard Run did an excellent job responding and attempting to clean up the oil in the early stages of the incident. This will be forwarded to WQS for follow up.

Violation ID: 982626
Permit API: 015-23700
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford

Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 1/24/2023
Comments: On 1/23/23 CHK reported a release of 42 gallons of produced water onto the pad surface. The release occurred around 11:00 on 1/23/23 when a produced water tank dump valve stuck open. It was estimated that the affected area was about 20' x 20'. The produced water tank was located on the northern side of the pad near the access road. At the time of inspection, the impacted area was revised to approximately 60' x 70' oriented north-south by east-west. The excavated area was approximately 10" - 12" deep. The excavation was being guided by conductivity measurements performed by Creston. The produced water tank will need to be moved in order to excavate the impacted area near the base and under the tank. The full depth of the excavation can not be determined until the tank is cleaned and moved, likely tomorrow 1/25/23.Conductivity measurements were taken around the the perimeter of the excavation. The measurements ranged from 0.02 to 0.390 millisiemens per centimeter (mS/cm). A roadside ditch running along the access road and leading to an infiltration basin below the produced water tank was also inspected and screened. The site was snow-covered and no visual evidence of runoff was noted. Soil conductivity readings were below 0.20 mS/cm.The result of the inspection is Violations Noted and Act 2 remediation will be pursued.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: RANGE RESOURCES APPALACHIA LLC

Violation Date: 7/13/2022
Violation Code: 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
Violation ID: 961490
Permit API: 081-20962
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: Cogan House Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 7/13/2022
Comments: On July 12, 2022, Range Resources Kirby Steck called DEP Brad Kline at 1430 to report that a water hauler was in the process of dewatering the production fluid tanks at the Porter Stephen Pad, when the hose from the water truck became obstructed and began leaking from an open bleeder valve of the truck. The bleeder valve leaked water outside of containment onto the well pad surface. Range Resources immediately mobilized equipment to the site to begin excavating the impacted soil. Mr. Steck called DEP at 1545 to update DEP on the removal of the impacted soil and to increase the estimate of the volume of production fluid spilled to approximately 2 barrels. On July 13, 2022, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted a site inspection at the Range Resources Porter Stephen Well Pad in response to a reported spill (CTS 365470) of 2 barrels of produced fluid from a water tank truck. At the time of inspection, Range Resources had excavated and area approximately 20 ft. by 20 ft. with a narrow 10 ft. area extending south from the main excavation. The spill occurred next to the containment for the production fluid tanks. DEP screened the excavation area with a soil conductivity meter. The screening resulted in finding 3 small areas that were over range of the soil conductivity meter. These areas were shown to Range Resources Kirby Steck when he arrived on site. Mr. Steck began hand digging these area as I left the site. There were three covered roll off dumpsters onsite filled with impacted soil. Mr. Steck said Moody and Associates are scheduled to be onsite to begin the Act 2 sampling and assessment on July 14, 2022. The spill of production fluid outside of containment to the well pad surface is a violation of Clean Streams Law 402(b), Chapter 78a.56(a), and Solid Waste Management Act Section 301.

Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 3/13/2025
Comments: On 03/13/2025 an Incident Response inspection was conducted at the DMC Well Site in response to an operator reported release.On 03/13/2025 Range Resources Representative, Dennis Furmanek, reported an approximately 84-gallon release of frack fluid off containment at the DMC Well pad located in Donegal Township, Washington County.Range Resources representative, Matthew Dorsey, was on site at the time of inspection. Mr. Dorsey informed the Department that the release was discovered today (03/13/2025) at approximately 5:00 am, that the quantity released was approximately 84 gallons, and that some of the fluid had since been removed via vacuum truck. The source of release was determined to be a hole in the manifold of a blender, located on the southwestern side of the well pad. The release occurred from the damaged blender, filled and overtopped the primary containment, filled and overtopped the secondary containment, and was release onto the pad aggregate. Mr. Dorsey stated that the cleanup will commence after the frac is completed and equipment is removed in approximately 8 days.Range Resources representative, Dennis Furmanek, contacted via phone call to provide updates. Mr. Furmanek stated that a large sump will be dug behind the spill site on the southwestern end of the well pad to collect any remaining fluids and remediation will begin next week after tear down is complete. He stated that he would notify the Department when the cleanup will begin.Mr. Furmanek also stated that he believed the elevated readings that were obtained from the driving lane on the eastern side of the pad and near the site entrance were caused from road salt that had been tracked onto the site from the large number of sand trucks. He stated that the area in which the elevated readings were observed was the same area in which the sand trucks consistently traveled and parked. He also stated the area had recently been sprayed with water to reduce the dust, which would explain the mud observed in those areas that were exhibiting elevated conductivity.Conductivity probe calibrated on 03/13/2025.The following was observed during the inspection:-The Act 9 sign was present at the site entrance. Various co-operations were taking place at the time of inspection and frac equipment was observed on site (Photos 1-2).-Large amounts of pooled fluid and mud were observed on a driving lane near the site entrance on the eastern side of the well pad. Elevated field conductivity readings of 3.37 ms/cm and 4.43 ms/cm were observed (Photos 3-8).-The mixer where the release originated, the secondary containments, and the surrounding areas were observed. The extent of impact could not be determined because much of the impacted area was located beneath the secondary containment. A small sump and hose were observed, located in the impacted area beneath the white plastic sheeting covering the temporary waterline. Field conductivity screening was conducted throughout the impacted area. Elevated field screening values ranged between 4.29 ms/cm and greater than 20 ms/cm. The discharge onto the ground and failure to dispose of fluids, specifically produced fluid, are violations of 78a.54, 78a.57(a), and Solid Waste Management Act (SWMA) 301. The potential to have indirectly impacted Waters of the Commonwealth (WOC) is a violation of 91.34(a) (Photos 4-16).-Pooled fluid was observed in tire tracks near the site entrance. Field conductivity screening was conducted throughout the area. Elevated field screening values of 2.48 ms/cm and 2.93 ms/cm were observed. Non-elevated field conductivity screening values of 78.5 s/cm and 1,189 s/cm were observed on either side of the temporary water line (Photos 17-20).Determination:Violations issued.

CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: STONEHAVEN ENERGY MGT CO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 5/15/2023
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 995073
Permit API: 053-29573
Unconventional: No
County: Forest
Municipality: Howe Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 5/15/2023
Comments: This conventional well is equipped with a pump jack. Neither the well operator or permit number is posted on the well or well site.This well is plumbed into a 2000 gallon plastic tank located next to the well. The upper portion of this tank is cracked/broken. This tank is approximately one-third full with production fluid from the well, including crude oil. There is no containment in place around this tank.The specific conductance (SPC) of the soil in the proximity of the valve for this tank and a smaller tote adjacent to the tank is elevated. In addition to elevated SPC, the soil is stained, vegetation is stressed and deer tracks are abundant near the tank and tote. The SPC of standing water and soil in the roadside ditch that runs next to the tank is also elevated for approximately 200 feet both to the north and south of the tank.The access road between this well and 053-29570 has not been properly maintained. As a result, the installed BMPs are not functional and accelerated erosion of the road surface has occurred. Numerous other sections of lease roads throughout the Warrant 2878 lease have also been neglected and are in need of repair/maintenance to be considered in compliance.Please see the attached Notice of Violation regarding requested information pertaining to the cause of the release and intentions to remediate the contaminated material at this well site.

Report Details

Violation ID: 906097
Permit API: 015-22632
Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 1/27/2021
Comments: On 01/27/2021, DEP representative John Ciccone visited Chesapeake Appalachia LLC (CALLC)'s McEnaney location in response to a spill notification (CTS # 354570). The initial spill notification was called in by Danielle Schaad (CALLC) on 01/26/2021. Ms. Schaad stated that approximately 7.5 gallons of production fluid was released to the pad surface during the replacement of a production fluid tank onsite. The cause of the spill was reported to be a result of the production fluid tank cracking during the cleaning / replacement process. Mountain Energy Services and Evergreen Oilfield Solutions was called in to respond to the site and to remediate the impacted area. I arrived onsite at 1002 hours. The weather was approximately 28 degrees Fahrenheit with overcast skies. The pad surface had approximately 1 inch of snow cover present. I investigated the area of release and found that the area had been scraped and impacted soils excavated and removed from the site. It appears the extent of the excavation was adequate in removing impacted soils. There were no puddles and/or melts present around the area of release noted at the time of this investigation. The slope of the pad immediately adjacent to the area of release was inspected for potential impact. The slope was found to have no obvious indications of production fluid release. The compromised production fluid tank remained onsite within a secondary containment. It appears the region of the tank wall that cracked had been patched via a tarp and duct tape. It was noted that the tape was beginning to peel away from the tank during the time of this inspection. I called Ms. Schaad at the conclusion of my site visit. I informed Ms. Schaad of the apparent peeling of the duct tape being used to patch the cracked production fluid tank. I asked Ms. Schaad when the compromised production fluid tank would be removed from the site. Ms. Schaad stated that the tank was scheduled to be removed from the site next Wednesday (02/03). Also noted, Ms. Schaad stated that less than 1 barrel of soils were excavated from the impacted area. The release of production fluids to the pad surface is in violation of Pa. Code 78a.56(a), CSL 402(b), and SWMA 301. Due to the reported quantity of the release (7.5 gallons) and the actions taken by CALLC to remediate the area of release, violations noted are considered immediately corrected. I departed the site at 1040 hours.

Comments: On 03/11/2024, a follow up inspection was conducted at the Molek F19 well site following violations issued on 12/08/2023 (IR 3657799, Enforcement 419234). I was accompanied by Environmental Trainees Olivia Holley, Madison Raviart, and Christina Mauri (PA DEP).On 12/08/2023, violations of 102.11(a), 102.22(a)2ii, and 78.53 were issued as outstanding for the access road. Inspection from 12/28/2023 noted that the violations were still open, however the operator was in compliance with schedule. On 01/24/2024, the violations were outstanding (IR 3701625). The following was observed:Some stabilization was used along the upper portion of the access road. Several areas throughout the entire access road did not have stabilization on the open soils. I recommend that stabilization is applied (Photos 1-4). Some areas had vegetation establishing (Photos 2, 4, 5).The channel that runs along the access road did not have rip rap or stabilization. Accelerated erosion and sediment accumulation were noted within this channel, which leads to several culverts along the road (Photo 6).The upper culvert, located at 40.113707 -79.966213, had sediment accumulation within the collection point. I recommend that this is addressed (Photo 7). The culvert located at 40.11300, -79.96751 had large amounts of sediment accumulated within the collection point. The culvert was not able to be seen due to the large amount of sediment within this area (Photos 8, 9). Accelerated erosion was noted within the accumulated sediment (Photo 9). Report Details
Inspection Client: SENECA RESOURCES CO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 3/29/2024
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 8183522
Permit API: 117-22231
Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga
Municipality: Middlebury Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 4/11/2024
Comments: On 4/11/2024, DEP representative John Rogers conducted a drilling/completions inspection at the Seneca Resource's Taft 851 well site located in Middlebury Township, Tioga County. It was 56 degrees, overcast and lightly raining when I arrived on location. When I arrived at the site, I met Seneca's Company man, Justin Green and HSE coordinator, Wayne Fletcher. Justin described current operations as follows: The Patterson 801 drilling rig is set up on site drilling production on four of five new wells. This rig arrived on site and started drilling on 3/31/2024. They were currently drilling the production section on the 76HU well and were in the process of drilling the curve, currently being at 11,228 feet. The lateral section will follow with the total depth expected to be 25,544 feet. Justin accompanied me on the site inspection. The rig and ancillary equipment were stationed on secondary containment. Chemicals were staged on secondary containment. There were 10 frac tanks on the northeast side of the rig staged in secondary containment, these being used for various drilling fluids. There were two frac tanks on the southeast side of the rig that were used to store rainwater collected from the pad surface. This water was being used for drilling fluids. The drill cuttings were being solidified with a plant-based substance called slate dry and with wood pellets prior to being transported offsite to a waste disposal facility. I did witness drill cuttings being piled up above the level of the exterior wall of an open top tank. I discussed keeping the level of the material low enough to allow for necessary free board.Due to recent rainfall, water puddles were present on the pad surface. I sampled a channel of water along the east side of the north perimeter berm that had demonstrated in prior inspections as having elevated levels of conductivity. The water field tested at 2.36 mS conductance near where a white residue could be seen on the gravel. The water field tested at 2.13 near the pad outfall in the center of the north perimeter berm and field tested at 2.11 mS as the water was running down the outfall. The water was flowing down to the northeast end of the sediment basin. The flow of water leading into the sediment basin field tested at 2.15mS conductance. Water leaving the sediment basin field tested at 0.869 mS conductance. Water flowing off location field tested at 0.88 mS conductance.No E and S issues were observed during the time of the inspection. Temporary compost filter socks have been installed throughout the construction site. I did witness emerging vegetation in the constructed areas but the requirements for permanent stabilization have not been met yet. Three sediment traps and one sediment basin have been installed on site and along the access road. They have not been converted to PCSM BMPs yet. Standing water was present in the basins.Violations are still outstanding for inspection ID 3724668 and ID 3736567 for a 6' x 60' puddle of water with elevated conductance and with a white substance in it; discovered on the unprotected pad surface and flowing into the sediment basin during drilling operations. The DEP recommends the following: 1. Continues the process of determining the source of contamination as witnessed in this and prior inspections. 2. Assess the area of elevated conductance fluid on the north side of the pad and entering the sediment basin. Clean and report as necessary.3. Maintain adequate levels of freeboard in open-topped containers including the half-round dumpsters being used for drill cuttings.4. Continue to monitor the stability and functionality of the sediment traps and sediment basin and repair as necessary.I left the site at 1300 hours.

Comments: The Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a ROUTINE inspection of the JKLM - Judson Hollow 302 Well Pad located in Pike Twp, Potter Co. on 10/21/2019 @1240 hours. The weather was 68 degrees and sunny. Profrac and JKLM were onsite performing stimulation activities on the 3HU well. During the course of the inspection, fluid was observed along northern edge of pad-wide containment. The fluid on the pad surface had a field measured conductivity of "Over Range" or >19.99mS/cm. The working tanks along the northern edge were in their own secondary containment. This containment had fluid with a field conductivity of 1200uS/cm. The working tank secondary containment was sitting within the pad-wide containment. This pad-wide containment was holding fluid with a field measured conductivity of "Over Range" or >19.99mS/cm. The fluid level appeared to be above the rig matting. Upon closer inspection with JKLM personnel, a hole/tear was discovered in the corner of pad-wide containment approximately half way down, releasing the fluid to the pad surface. Sample 4427-193 was collected from the "Over Range" fluid on the pad surface. JKLM immediately propped up the tank containment to allow vac truck hoses to begin removing the fluid from the pad-wide containment where the tear was located. The area where the fluid was visible on the pad surface was cordoned off to keep traffic from tracking the fluid onto other areas of the well pad. The Operator also contacted the containment company to initiate repair. I received email confirmation from the Operator that as of 1800 hours the spill had been remediated. The email states, "Once puddles were recovered, soil in the impacted area was screened for specific conductance on a 12'x12' grid (see pre-excavation screening drawing). Damp pad material was then removed to a depth of between 1-2" and placed in a 20 yd. dumpster (OT 048). Post-excavation soil screening readings were then obtained (the highest reading was 1.23 mS/cm). The cleanup was complete by 1800 hrs." Violations of the following regulations are cited against the 3HU well, API#105-21922, as IMMEDIATELY CORRECTED. CSL 402(b) SWMA 301 25 Pa Code 78a.56(a)
